approved: Transport Security Amendment (Security of Australia’s Transport Sector) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would update Australia's aviation and maritime security laws to address current and emerging threats such as cyber incidents and natural hazards.
It would broaden the definition of unlawful interference, introduce all-hazards security obligations, and add new testing powers for the maritime sector.
The bill would also enable a demerit points scheme for aviation and require yearly compliance statements from industry participants.
Amends the definition of unlawful interference to include cyber security incidents and, for maritime, attempted acts.
Introduces all-hazards security obligations and the concept of operational interference.
Requires aviation industry participants to conduct a security assessment and submit a yearly Statement of Compliance.
Introduces system testing and vulnerability testing for the maritime sector.
Broadens and aligns security direction provisions in maritime law with aviation law.
Enables a future demerit points scheme for aviation in regulations.
Regulated industry participants in the aviation and maritime transport sectors.

Moved procedural arrangements to sequence debate and votes on Supply Bills, the Transport Security Amendment Bill 2024, the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment Bill 2025 and the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2025. Said the motion was needed because Senate estimates would prevent later consideration.

Supported the Transport Security Amendment (Security of Australia's Transport Sector) Bill 2024 and government amendments, arguing that it would strengthen aviation and maritime security through broader unlawful-interference definitions, mandatory cybersecurity reporting and an all-hazards framework. Sought consultation for 12 months and a 24-month transition period, particularly for regional airports.

Reported that debate time had expired under an earlier resolution and put the questions required to complete consideration of the listed bills; the question was agreed to and the bill was read a second time.

Presented an advisory report on the Transport Security Amendment (Security of Australia's Transport Sector) Bill 2024 and moved that the Senate take note. Reported that evolving cyber, foreign interference, espionage, terrorism and supply-chain risks required reform, while recommending clearer guidance, reduced regulatory duplication, safeguards and support for smaller entities.

Moved and amended a Senate business motion setting meeting hours, ordering consideration and expedited voting on listed bills, providing for valedictory statements and budget responses, allowing divisions after 6.30 pm, and adding further bills before the motion was agreed to.

Presented an advisory report on the Transport Security Amendment (Security of Australia's Transport Sector) Bill 2024, identifying cyber, organised crime, terrorism and foreign interference risks and recommending consultation, reduced regulatory duplication, scalable penalties, safeguards and more time for smaller entities before supporting passage.
